ai.literal: Without not-forming of-excellence even if they are, to-diminish things-that-come abandoning.
ai.translation: One must abandon actions that diminish one's honor, even if they bring indispensable greatness.
ai.modern: ஒரு செயல் இல்லாமல் முடியாத சிறப்பைத் தருவதாக இருந்தாலும், தன் மானம் குறையும்படி வரும் அச்செயலை விட்டுவிட வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: The idiom 'இன்றி அமையா' describes something that is absolutely indispensable or essential. The couplet advises that even if an action promises such essential greatness or immense benefits, it must be rejected if it compromises one's dignity. The word 'குன்ற' means to diminish, referring here to the lowering of one's honor. Thus, 'வருப விடல்' commands the abandonment of any incoming deeds or gains that would reduce one's self-respect.

ai.literal: Even in greatness, greatness-not-things they will not do indeed, with greatness great-manliness those who desire.
ai.translation: Those who desire great honor along with lasting glory will not do inglorious deeds, even if it brings them greatness.
ai.modern: புகழோடு கூடிய சிறந்த மானத்தை விரும்புபவர்கள், தமக்கு பெரும் புகழ் கிடைப்பதாக இருந்தாலும், புகழுக்கு ஒவ்வாத இழிவான செயல்களைச் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes that true honor cannot be compromised for the sake of temporary success or glory. The word பேராண்மை (great manliness) here refers to the supreme strength of character that upholds dignity. Those who seek such noble character along with true greatness will never commit degrading acts, even if those acts promise to elevate their status.

ai.literal: In prosperity is needed humility; in small reduction is needed elevation.
ai.translation: In times of prosperity, one needs humility. In times of decline, one needs to maintain high dignity.
ai.modern: செல்வம் பெருகும் காலத்தில் பணிவு வேண்டும்; செல்வம் சுருங்கி வறுமை வரும் காலத்தில் தாழ்ந்து போகாத உயர்வான குணம் வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts how one should behave in good and bad times. During prosperity, a person should practice humility to avoid arrogance. Conversely, during a reduction in wealth or status, one must maintain elevation and dignity to avoid losing self-respect. True honor lies in balancing modesty when wealthy with unyielding self-worth when poor.

ai.literal: From the head fallen hair like-they people, from standing fallen when.
ai.translation: When people fall from their honorable standing, they are like hair that has fallen from the head.
ai.modern: மக்கள் தம் உயர்ந்த நிலையிலிருந்து தாழ்ந்தால், அவர்கள் தலையிலிருந்து உதிர்ந்த மயிரைப் போன்றவர்கள் ஆவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a striking simile to explain the loss of honor. Hair is carefully groomed and valued as long as it remains on the head, but becomes worthless dirt the moment it falls. Similarly, people are respected when they maintain their dignity and moral standing, but lose all their worth when they fall from that honorable state.

ai.literal: Even those who are like a mountain will shrink, if they do degrading things like a kunri seed.
ai.translation: Even those whose greatness towers like a mountain will be diminished if they commit a degrading act as small as a kunri seed.
ai.modern: மலை போல உயர்ந்த பெருமை உடையவர்களும், குன்றிமணி அளவு சிறியதான இழிவான செயல்களைச் செய்தால் தமது பெருமையில் தாழ்ந்து போவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the massive size of a mountain with the tiny size of a kunri seed to illustrate the fragility of honor. Even people of towering, mountain-like greatness will lose their stature if they commit a shameful act. The poet emphasizes that the degrading act does not need to be large; even a flaw as small as a tiny seed is enough to ruin a great reputation.

ai.literal: Fame is not indeed; in the gods' world it does not save indeed; what then [is the use of] behind despisers having gone standing?
ai.translation: Standing as a follower behind those who despise you brings no fame here, nor does it secure a place in the world of the gods. What then is its use?
ai.modern: தன்னை அவமதிப்பவர்களின் பின்னால் சென்று கைகட்டி நிற்கும் நிலையானது ஒருவனுக்கு இவ்வுலகில் புகழையும் தராது, தேவர் உலகிலும் இடமளிக்காது. அப்படியிருக்க அதனால் வேறு என்ன பயன்?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the value of sacrificing one's honor to seek favors from those who show contempt. The phrase 'இகழ்வார் பின் சென்று நிலை' (standing behind those who despise) captures the humiliating act of following scornful people. The poet argues that such behavior yields no worldly 'புகழ்' (fame or respect). Furthermore, it 'உய்யாதால்' (does not save or uplift) one to the 'புத்தேள் நாட்டு' (world of the gods). Since it offers neither earthly glory nor heavenly reward, the couplet concludes by asking 'என் மற்று' (what else is it good for?), emphasizing that abandoning self-respect is utterly pointless.

ai.translation: It is better to be known as one who perished right where he stood, than to live by following behind one's foes.
ai.modern: பகைவர்களின் பின்னே சென்று ஒருவன் உயிர்வாழ்வதை விட, தன் மானம் அழியும் நிலை வந்தபோதே அவன் இறந்துவிட்டான் என்று சொல்லப்படுவது அவனுக்கு மிகவும் நல்லதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of honor over mere survival. It states that living a life of humiliation by trailing behind one's enemies is worse than death. The phrase 'அந்நிலையே கெட்டான்' highlights that perishing in one's current honorable state, without compromising dignity, is far superior. Thus, true life is defined by self-respect, and losing it makes physical survival meaningless.

ai.literal: Is it an elixir, indeed, flesh-cherishing life, great dignity's honor to be destroyed when it has come?
ai.translation: When great dignity and honor are destroyed, is a life that merely cherishes the physical body an elixir of immortality?
ai.modern: தமது பெருமையும் மானமும் அழியும்படியான நிலை வந்தபோது, உடம்பை மட்டும் காப்பாற்றி வாழும் வாழ்க்கை என்ன சாகா வரம் தரும் மருந்தா?
ai.explanation: This couplet questions the value of clinging to physical survival at the cost of one's honor. The word 'ஊன்' (flesh) emphasizes the mere physical body, contrasting it with 'பெருந்தகைமை பீடு' (the honor of great dignity). The poet asks rhetorically if a life that merely protects the flesh is an elixir of immortality ('மருந்தோ'). It implies that since the body will eventually die anyway, sacrificing one's honor just to prolong physical existence is foolish and unworthy of a noble person.

ai.literal: Hair if removed not-living kavari-animal those-who-are-like, life they-will-remove honor if-comes.
ai.translation: Those who are like the kavari animal, which cannot live if it loses its hair, will give up their lives if an affront to their honor comes.
ai.modern: தன் உடலிலிருந்து மயிர் நீங்கினால் உயிர் வாழாத கவரிமானைப் போன்றவர்கள், தங்கள் மானத்திற்கு ஒரு குறை வந்தால் உயிரையே விட்டுவிடுவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares honorable people to the legendary kavari animal (often identified as the yak), which is said to die if it loses its hair. The word 'kavarimā' denotes this specific animal, while 'vāḻā' emphasizes its inability to survive the loss of its defining feature. Similarly, for people of true honor, their dignity is as vital as life itself. If a situation arises where their honor is compromised ('māṉam variṉ'), they will readily give up their life ('uyir nīppar') rather than live in disgrace.

ai.literal: Disgrace if comes who do not live, honor those who possess - glory having bowed will praise the world.
ai.translation: The world will bow down and praise the glory of honorable people who will not survive if disgrace befalls them.
ai.modern: தமக்கு ஒரு சிறுமை வந்தால் உயிரோடு வாழாத மானம் உடையவர்களின் புகழை, இந்த உலகம் தொழுது போற்றும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the ultimate standard of personal dignity. The word 'இளி' means disgrace or indignity, representing anything that compromises one's self-respect. The word 'ஒளி' literally means light, but in this context, it is best understood as the radiant glory or lasting fame of the honorable. The text states that those who possess true dignity will not continue to live if they face such disgrace. Because of this unwavering commitment to their honor, the world will bow down and praise their brilliant legacy.
